title: The 0.1 custom-profile status enum is unreachable once the built-in lifecycle enum runs at load (DEC-192 consequence)
description:
Consequence of DEC-192 (LCLI-669). The built-in lifecycle enum now runs on ADR documents on OKF 0.1 as well as 0.2, so a 0.1 custom profile declaring a NON-BUILT-IN status enum (for example [draft, approved]) can only ever use draft on an ADR: every other value is rejected at LOAD by the built-in enum, so the write-time custom-enum validation that profile was written for is never exercised. Meanwhile the profile still EMITS a 0.1 schema declaring its own custom enum, so the declared schema and the enforced behaviour disagree.

test/supersede.test.ts:456 passes for the wrong reason because of this -- status: approved is rejected by the built-in enum at LOAD, not by the custom enum at WRITE.

HELD, do not start. The resolution is a design choice for opum-doc: either the built-in lifecycle enum defers to a project's declared enum where one exists, or a project enum must include the built-in values, or the 0.1 carve-out is widened. Reported, not settled, exactly as the task rule requires.
plan: profile.ts: BUILTIN_LIFECYCLE_STATUS and effectiveLifecycleStatusEnum (the declared `status` enum, else the built-in); compiled per type as lifecycleStatusEnum, plus supersededStatus from the type new superseded_status key
schema.ts: validateLifecycleStatus reads the compiled type effective enum, and schemaForVersion 0.2 `status` property emits the SAME enum; the built-in remedy is kept for a profile that declares none
profile.ts parseProfile: refuse BY NAME a superseded_status outside the type effective enum (and an empty one); it stays out of declaredFields and the emitted schema
supersede.ts: resolveSupersededStatus writes `deprecated` when the effective enum has it, else the type superseded_status, else refuses by name quoting the enum and the key
Proofs with mutation controls in test/effective-status-enum.test.ts, test/profile.test.ts, test/supersede.test.ts -- each check broken and the predicted subset confirmed red
Docs: DEFAULT_PROFILE_TOML (the profile reference `lore init` writes) documents the key; CHANGELOG entries under Unreleased
implementationNotes:
DEC-192 (4) READ BY REF (opum-doc origin/dev .quest/planning.json), 2026-10-14: the project's declared ADR status enum takes precedence. (1)'s principle was always "an ADR's status must be inside the enum its own bundle's schema declares"; the built-in [draft, stable, deprecated] was the evidence because it is the DEFAULT. So the effective enum is the profile's declared one when it declares one, and the built-in when it declares none. The emitted schema and the runtime check must read the SAME enum -- that is the defect: a custom [draft, approved] profile emitted its own enum while load enforced the built-in.
- lore supersede writes the effective enum's superseded value: "deprecated" when that is in the effective enum; otherwise the profile declares which value marks a superseded ADR (an ADR-type profile key, e.g. superseded_status), and supersede refuses BY NAME, quoting the profile's enum and the key to set, when neither applies. It never writes an out-of-enum value.
- Proofs: a [draft, approved] profile accepts "approved" on an ADR and refuses "stable"; the default profile still refuses "superseded"; supersede on a custom profile with no superseded value refuses by name; and test/supersede.test.ts:456 passes for the right reason.

PLAN (branch feat/LCLI-723-effective-status-enum off dev 833e6b5e): (a) an effective-enum helper reading the profile's DECLARED `status` spec, which is already the source the emitted schema uses (profile.ts baseKindToZod); (b) validateLifecycleStatus (schema.ts) reading THAT instead of the hard-coded LIFECYCLE_STATUS_SCHEMA; (c) supersede writing the effective superseded value, never an out-of-enum one; (d) the four proofs above.

OPEN SHAPE QUESTION (reported to the leader, not settled here): "an ADR-type profile key, for example superseded_status" -- is it (i) a key ON THE ADR TYPE beside fields/sections (a NEW key in the published profile contract, and whether it is emitted into adr.schema.json), or (ii) a declared concept-field whose enum member marks supersession? (i) reads as what the words mean, but adding a key to the published profile contract is not the worker's to settle.

HANDOFF — session renewal, 2026-10-14. This session is being renewed onto a fresh one; the leader's instruction is that the successor BUILDS LCLI-723 in one pass from this record plus the ruling, so this note is the whole brief.

STATE. Branch feat/LCLI-723-effective-status-enum (this branch) off dev 833e6b5e, one commit cb6c1023 carrying the claim, the DEC-192 (4) reading and the plan. dev has moved on since (#585 landed as b2b6d00f) — MERGE DEV BEFORE GATING, the practice this session had to learn three times.

SETTLED — DEC-192 (4), opum-ai/opum-doc#1010, read by ref here (.quest/planning.json on opum-doc origin/dev), not from a relay: the effective status enum is the profile's DECLARED `status` enum when it declares one, else the built-in [draft, stable, deprecated], and the emitted schema and the runtime load check must read the SAME enum. That disagreement IS the defect: FieldSpec.enum feeds the emitted schema at profile.ts baseKindToZod, while load hard-codes LIFECYCLE_STATUS_SCHEMA at schema.ts validateLifecycleStatus. supersede writes the effective enum's superseded value — "deprecated" when that value is in the enum — and never an out-of-enum value.

WHAT BLOCKED IT, and it is still open: the same ruling adds "otherwise the profile declares which value marks a superseded ADR (an ADR-type profile key, for example superseded_status)". Whether that is a key ON THE ADR TYPE — an addition to the published profile CONTRACT — or a declared concept field is a DESIGN question, and the leader has ROUTED IT TO opum-doc. DO NOT GUESS IT. Wait for the relayed ruling before writing that half; the rest is ready.

PROOFS THE RULING REQUIRES: a [draft, approved] profile accepts "approved" on an ADR and refuses "stable"; the default profile still refuses "superseded"; supersede on a custom profile with no superseded value refuses BY NAME, quoting the enum and the key to set; and test/supersede.test.ts:456 passes for the right reason rather than because load rejected it first.

REACH FOR: the opum-sdlc skill for branch/PR/close, its references/quest-writes.md for the tracker traps, and opum-handoff restore on resume. Run `lore check` on the MERGED state, never the branch alone — LCLI-726, filed this session, exists to make that automatic.

QUEUE BEHIND THIS: LCLI-727 (the LCLI-670 follow-up task, landed in the tracker), LCLI-726 (the merged-state gate), LCLI-722 (the profile reshape that removes the capacity pressure this session kept hitting).

DEC-192 (6) READ BY REF (opum-doc origin/dev .quest/planning.json; opum-ai/opum-doc#1018, MERGED), 2026-10-14: `superseded_status` is a key ON THE ADR TYPE in the profile, beside `fields` and `sections` -- e.g. { name = "ADR", superseded_status = "approved" }. (a) At profile load it must be a member of the effective status enum, or the load refuses BY NAME. (b) It is NOT emitted into adr.schema.json (profile configuration, not a document field). (c) The profile reference documents it as a published key. (d) supersede's refusal names it when it is needed and absent.

READING, recorded because "the profile reference" is not a file in docs/: resolved to the fully-commented `.lore/profile.toml` template `lore init` writes -- src/core/scaffold.ts DEFAULT_PROFILE_TOML. It is the ONLY artifact in this repository that enumerates the published profile keys ([profile], [base.fields], [[types]] name/sections/template/fields); docs/reference has no profile-format page, and the string `[[types]]` appears nowhere under docs/ except adr/0007. Consequence: the documentation lands in a scaffolded file, not a docs page, so no agent-profile-pinned source grows (LCLI-702 capacity).

PLAN, restated against the rulings: (a) profile.ts owns BUILTIN_LIFECYCLE_STATUS plus effectiveLifecycleStatusEnum(statusSpec) -- the declared `status` enum when the type declares one, else the built-in triple; stored per compiled type as lifecycleStatusEnum. (b) schema.ts validateLifecycleStatus reads THAT instead of the hard-coded LIFECYCLE_STATUS_SCHEMA, and schemaForVersion's 0.2 `status` property emits the SAME effective enum, so emitted schema and runtime check can no longer disagree. (c) ParsedType/CompiledType gain superseded_status/supersededStatus; parseProfile refuses at load, by name, a value outside the type's effective enum; it stays out of the emitted schema because buildJsonSchema reads FIELDS only. (d) supersede writes the effective superseded value: `deprecated` when it is in the enum, else the type's superseded_status, else it refuses by name quoting the enum and the key. (e) Proofs, each with a mutation control.
